correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly establishes the expansion/endomorphism bijection, finite Birkhoff duality, fixed-subset criterion, labeled transition, orbit transition and closed-form solutions. Experiments are presented only as finite consistency tests; the unrestricted finite statements follow from the proof.

originality.rationale: The novelty assessed is the two-state exact labeled and isomorphism-class counting recurrence for strong subresiduated expansions on every ordinal sum of finite antichains. The general correspondence between poset idempotents and image sets is demonstrably prior art and explicitly credited; the 2023 variety paper defines the algebraic class. Inspected primary results and targeted research records did not exhibit this specialized exact recurrence or a stronger direct formula. The record acknowledges closely related prior branching algorithms, source-access limitations and residual alternative-formulation risk.
residual_risks: Two close recent published record full texts could not be accessed; their abstracts do not resolve every possible stronger equivalent theorem.
Generic Denton branching readily specializes to finite weak orders, so any claim of novelty is confined to the derived compressed exact labeled and orbit formulas, not the fixed-point-set principle.
A differently named prior enumeration of order-preserving regressive idempotents on layered posets may exist outside searched material.

value.rationale: An exact, family-wide algebraic-logical census is mathematically natural because finite upset lattices arise in representations of the strong subresiduated variety. The two weighted transfer matrices count all labeled expansions and isomorphism types for arbitrary positive layer size vectors with O(h) arithmetic, replacing exponentially large generic image-set enumeration. Uniform rank profiles yield closed all-height forms; this is not an arbitrary small numerical slice or a claim about previously unknown integer sequences.
